Dear Dr. Miller,

Thank you for seeing Mr. Arthur Vance, a 65-year-old gentleman who presented to our clinic for a comprehensive ophthalmic consultation. He is a retired teacher, a non-smoker, and is currently taking no prescription medications. His general physical review and vital signs were entirely unremarkable today.

On examination, his best-corrected visual acuity was bilaterally subnormal, measuring 20/100 in each eye. Sensorimotor alignment showed a manifest inward deviation of the left eye; no exotropia was observed during cover testing. A low-amplitude, horizontal involuntary oscillation of the globes was readily apparent in primary gaze. 

Slit-lamp biomicroscopy revealed pale blue irides with distinct transillumination defects visible through the mid-peripheral iris stroma. Corneas and lenses were clear. External inspection demonstrated notable pigmentary changes: his eyelashes and both eyebrows are completely white, accompanied by very lightly pigmented, silvery-blonde scalp hair. A small, clinically benign mole was also noted over his left malar prominence. On dilated posterior segment examination, the optic nerve heads and peripheral vasculature were normal, but macula-line scans confirmed an absence of the normal central foveal depression bilaterally. 

I would be most grateful for your specialized evaluation and recommendations regarding his overall ocular management and visual support.

Sincerely,

Dr. Julian Croft
